original_results_policy: Keep prior corpus, protocol, predictions, calibration, locks and results unchanged. Report this independent supplement separately; never select a favorable corpus or label order after held-out inference.
purpose: Repair the declared template coverage ceiling and single-class owner/name calibration contexts without relaxing acceptance thresholds.

corpus.translation_policy: The three language variants share a group and split. Reordered-label variants stay with the originating meeting.
corpus.content_isolation: Each split has its own topic, follow-up action objects, quantity ranges, deadlines and authored statement families. Topic context is present in inference state, not only metadata. No verbatim state or target-evidence text is reused across splits. Question instructions and candidate descriptions intentionally remain stable for calibration.
corpus.source: Authored synthetic short meeting fragments only; no private recordings or model outputs.
corpus.name_scope: Names are restricted to a fixed candidate list and established by direct self-introduction. This does not test open-vocabulary extraction or acoustic speaker recognition.

calibration.context_policy: Use existing full identity/route/privacy, precision, prompt, ordered-label, question-grouping and language context rules. Preserve each order separately. No held-out threshold tuning.

acceptance.scope: Apply original protocol thresholds independently per language; report raw and frozen-calibrated results and every error/abstention.
acceptance.combination: Supplement owner results and original event-kind results may inform a structured-task recommendation, but independent classifiers do not establish measured end-to-end structured extraction.

budgets.execution_policy: Explicit evaluation configuration only; preserve existing spend and reservations. Commit corpus/protocol/prompt/model/route/config hashes before held-out inference.

limitations: This repair follows an observed design feasibility problem and is a new preregistered experiment, not an untouched original holdout.
Controlled synthetic grammar and fixed candidate names are not natural-meeting or device acceptance; procedural grammar transfer remains limited even with split-specific wording and event facts.
Calibration samples remain small. Twelve meeting groups per task/order/language support the declared minimum, not a broad statistical guarantee.
Bounded supplement inputs do not replace prior long-input refusals or prove full-context support.
